newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - US debt vols flat to easier, await data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - US debt vols flat to easier, await data.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. fixed income options were steady to easier, despite nervousness ahead of Friday's December U.S. employment report, dealers said.

Bids for options appeared to have waned somewhat after an early rally in underlying markets triggered by benign readings in the December U.S. producer price index, they said. They added that those who wanted to be long options ahead of the report had already built up positions.
"They're coming in a little bit off the (PPI) numbers," said a T-bond trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.
He noted that volatilities have recently tended to start firming up a week or two prior to the jobs data day and start eroding a day or two prior to the numbers.
Implied volatilities for February and March T-bond futures options were a fraction lower than Wednesday's closing levels at 10.7 and 10.3 percent respectively.

Early in the pit session, bond prices dipped and then quickly rebounded after the PPI figures. While the overall PPI came in slightly higher than anticipated, the market in the end perceived the prices data to be showing a benign inflation picture on the whole.

The overall PPI rose 0.5 percent in December against an average Wall Street estimate of a 0.3 percent rise and November's 0.4 percent gain. The core rate, excluding food and energy, rose 0.1 percent, unchanged from November and in line with expectations.
Still, the market remained generally cautious, given the wild swings it had experienced on jobs data days last year.
"The market's bounced back really well, but it won't mean a thing going into tomorrow's number," said a Eurodollar trader for a brokerage firm at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
Economists polled by Reuters have forecast on average an increase of 192,000 in December non-farm payrolls, compared with a rise of 118,000 in November.
Implied volatility for CME June Eurodollar futures options was virtually unchanged at about 13.5 percent, while September was off some 0.2 point to 15.7 percent.
Overall volume was moderate although there were few large deals, unlike the past few days, a trader at a bank affiliate at CME said.
